# Interactive meta-prompt (generated by the mini-program)

The template behind the 「复制整理说明」 button. **English, deliberately minimal.**
It carries only two things, both **split into labelled parts** (never a bare URL, never an opaque blob):

1. the **skill document address**;
2. a **one-time authorization link**.

> 🔴 **Always reply to the user in Simplified Chinese**, even though this prompt is English.

---

## 1. The template (substitute the four placeholders, then hand it to the teacher)

```text
Skill document - join the two parts and read it:
  skillDoc.host : {docHost}
  skillDoc.path : {docPath}

One-time authorization link - single use, do not share:
  authLink.host : {authHost}
  authLink.path : {authPath}

Always reply to me in Chinese (简体中文).
Start now: read the skill document, then greet me.
```

**Join rule:** `https://` + `host` + `/` + `path`. Nothing else is transformed.

Example of how the two parts look once filled:

```text
  skillDoc.host : raw.githubusercontent.com
  skillDoc.path : Golinoa/yunce-meta-prompt/main/SKILL.md
```

---

## 2. Variables

| Placeholder | Meaning | Substituted by |
|---|---|---|
| `{docHost}` | host part of the skill document address | backend (lets ops switch to a Gitee mirror without touching this text) |
| `{docPath}` | path part of the skill document address | backend |
| `{authHost}` | host part of the **one-time** authorization link | server, at the moment the teacher taps 「复制」 |
| `{authPath}` | path part of the one-time authorization link (the credential lives here) | server, same moment |

### Why there is **no** `{apiBase}`

Deliberately removed. Handing an AI a base URL lets it assemble **any** endpoint path on that host —
an open over-reach surface. After the handshake succeeds, the **server returns `apiBase`** in the
response, and only then are downstream endpoints known.

### Why the addresses are split, **not** base64-encoded

An earlier version of this project hid a URL inside an opaque base64 blob and asked the AI to decode
and execute it. Content filters flagged that as **prompt injection** and some AIs refused to help.
Three things trigger that verdict:

1. impersonating a system message;
2. demanding **verbatim** execution of a remote file;
3. hiding the target behind an opaque encoding.

So this design uses **mild obfuscation only**: split the address into clearly **labelled parts**
that read like ordinary configuration fields. The AI still plainly understands
"read this document" / "call this link" — **no filter trips, no functionality lost.**

> Rule of thumb: **obfuscate the shape, never the intent.**

---

## 3. Security posture

- 🔴 **No real value ever enters this repo.** This file stores placeholders only.
- 🔴 **Never commit a real `{authHost}` / `{authPath}`.**
- Permission never comes from the prompt. It comes **only** from the teacher's login state plus the
  short code the server issues inside the mini-program. A fully leaked prompt grants **no write access**.
- The authorization link is **valid 1 hour if unused**, **burned on first successful call**.
  A second batch requires copying a fresh one.

---

## 4. Copy-time UX (mini-program side)

1. Teacher taps the copy entry → **confirmation dialog first** (neutral wording, **no AI-related terms**):
   > 这份整理说明**只能使用一次**，且会绑定你的账号，请勿转发。确认复制？
2. After confirming, the server issues the one-time link and the front-end renders the template,
   then copies it.

---

## 5. Ops

The **live** copy of this template lives in the ops backend (`运营 / legacy-import-settings`),
**not** in this repo. This file is the source of truth; update the backend by hand.
See `docs/ops-checklist.md`.
